executive_summary: Replace continuous arcade-style simulation with turn-based, step-through educational tool. Focus on clarity over spectacle. Show economic mechanisms explicitly.

key_features.name: Round-based execution
key_features.description: Click 'Run Round' button to execute one market period
key_features.rationale: Lets students see before/after, understand causation

key_features.name: Pre-round agent display
key_features.description: Show all agents' WTP/WTA as dots on supply/demand curve BEFORE trading
key_features.rationale: Makes supply/demand curves concrete - they're not abstract, they're actual agents

key_features.name: Animated market clearing
key_features.description: Show matching process: highest WTP buyer + lowest WTA seller = trade

key_features.name: Post-round analysis
key_features.description: Highlight completed trades, show surplus created, update stats

key_features.name: Agent inspector panel
key_features.description: Click any agent → see utility function, budget constraint, optimal choice
key_features.rationale: Shows micro foundations, connects individual behavior to market outcomes

key_features.name: Scenario library
key_features.description: Pre-built scenarios: 'Show deadweight loss', 'Demonstrate price ceiling', etc

remove: Phaser game engine (overkill, causes performance issues)
add: SVG for agent dots on curves
CSS transitions for smooth UI updates

after_trade: Show who traded, who didn't, and why
Update supply/demand curves with remaining agents

performance_solution.solution: Simple DOM/Canvas rendering, no game engine
performance_solution.expected_result: Instant updates, smooth on any device

questions_for_consensus: Should we keep any continuous animation, or go fully turn-based?
How many agents per round? (fewer = clearer, more = realistic)
Should agents persist across rounds or reset each time?
Do we need multiple market structures, or focus on perfect competition first?

estimated_effort.recommendation: Complete rewrite - current approach is fundamentally misaligned with educational goals
